correctness.rationale: Hagis--Lord's lower bound reduces the five-prime minimum to integer targets \(10,11,12,13\). For a fixed target, monotonicity of \(x/(x+1)\) gives a proved finite upper bound on each ordered prime-power component. After four choices, the fifth component is forced by \(Px/(x+1)=h/32\), so exact integrality, prime-power, order, and distinct-base checks are necessary and sufficient. The bundled exact rational recursion therefore exhausts all cases: none for 10--12 and exactly the two stated component sets for 13.
